old_caption: The video showcases a close-up view of an open tackle box, revealing its organized compartments filled with various fishing lures and accessories. The tackle box is predominantly blue and gray, with multiple sections designed to hold different types of fishing gear. The top compartment contains several small, colorful lures, including green, red, and metallic ones, neatly arranged on hooks. Below these, there are additional compartments holding more lures and possibly some fishing line or other small tools. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, focusing on the detailed contents of the tackle box. The background is slightly blurred, emphasizing the tackle box and its contents. There are no visible characters or animals in the scene, and the setting appears to be outdoors, possibly near a body of water given the context of the tackle box. The lighting suggests it might be daytime, with natural light illuminating the scene.

caption: The video showcases an open fishing tackle box in a close, slightly high view, its blue shell holding a gray inner tray with blue dividers and two blue hinge arms. The tray is already propped fully raised, so it never opens or closes in the visible span, and every lure sits undisturbed in its compartment. A green spinner, a red jig, a pink-and-silver crankbait, and a lime soft lure fill the cells, while a leafy plant pokes into the left edge. The background stays a soft blur of outdoor ground and leaf litter. During the clip the box and its contents hold their positions, with no sliding, lifting, or rattling of the tray on its hinges. The only visible motion is a slow drift of the scene, as the tray's lower lip and the left plant settle a few percent lower. This reads as a gentle handheld tilt or slight zoom rather than any action on the box. The arrangement stays unchanged throughout, resting open under the camera.

Distinguish an already ongoing process from a new event actually visible within this excerpt.
Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.

timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
